history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Medak Cathedral is a Christian (Church of South India) cathedral, not a Hindu temple. Built 1914-1924 under Rev. Charles Walker Posnett of the British Wesleyan Methodists on 1,000 acres in the Ghusnabad area; construction gave famine-relief employment ('food for work') during the 1919-1921 famine instead of a free kitchen. Consecrated 25 December 1924. From 1924-1947 it was the Wesleyan Methodist Church; it became the cathedral of the Diocese of Medak when the Church of South India formed in October 1947. Gothic Revival structure, 200 ft x 100 ft, 175 ft bell tower, capacity ~5,000; mosaic tiles imported from Britain laid by Italian masons from Bombay; three major stained-glass windows (Nativity, Crucifixion, Ascension) installed 1927-1958. Seat of the Medak diocese, claimed as Asia's largest and the world's second largest diocese after the Vatican (diocese claim unverified).

name: Medak Church
town_description: Medak is a historic town and district headquarters in northern Telangana, about 100 km from Hyderabad. It is known for the Medak Fort (Kakatiya-era) and the Medak Cathedral; the name Medak is said to derive from 'methuku' (cooked rice) in Telugu.
